result: The new HEK-GT and BHK-eT packaging cell lines enable production of RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c vectors with orders of magnitude higher titers, significantly reduced production time (rescue: 5-6 days vs 10-11 days; pseudotyping: 4-6 days vs 28 days), and minimal background contamination compared to previous methods.
evaluation: Claims C1, C3, C17-C24, and C31 collectively demonstrate the improved production system. The data in Figure 1H shows quantitative titer comparisons, Tables 1 and 2 provide timeline comparisons, and Figure 1F-G show amplification kinetics. The cell line design using antibiotic selection and co-expression of TVA/envA is well-documented with supporting data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

result: The new packaging system produces vectors with minimal background contamination (maximum 1-2 cells per 0.5-1 mm tissue in 37 batches tested), with sparse non-specific labeling only occurring at extremely high titers (100-500-fold above working concentrations) due to physical damage during injection rather than native-coat particle contamination.
evaluation: Claims C2, C25-C29 are supported by systematic testing of 37 viral batches (C25) and mechanistic experiments in organotypic cultures (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C-E) demonstrating that non-specific labeling results from tissue damage rather than contamination. The experimental design appropriately tests the hypothesis with temporal controls.

result: Vectors produced with the new BHK-eT system maintain comparable retrograde labeling efficiency to N2A-produced CVS-N2c vectors and show significantly higher efficiency than SAD B19 vectors, with specific and exclusive transduction of TVA-expressing starter cells.
evaluation: Claims C4, C32-C35, C37, C76-C77 are supported by multiple experimental validations shown in Figures 2 and 3. The side-by-side comparison in Figure 3 using dual-color labeling provides direct quantitative evidence, and the control experiments in Figure 2C demonstrate specificity. The statistical analysis in Figure 3H shows clear differences between CVS-N2c and SAD B19.

result: CVS-N2c vectors produced in BHK-eT cells label approximately 5-20 fold more 2nd order neurons than SAD B19 in most brain regions tested (CA3: ~14%, LEC: ~8%), except in medial septum where ratios were similar (~100%), with actual differences likely higher when using endogenous N2cG instead of oG.
evaluation: Claims C38-C40 are supported by quantitative data in Figure 3E-H showing clear differences in labeling efficiency. The exception for MS projections is noted and discussed. Figure 3—figure supplement 1 provides additional evidence for the glycoprotein effect. Sample sizes (n=3-4 animals) are adequate for the observed effect sizes.

result: Retrograde labeling from dentate gyrus revealed previously unreported hippocampal projections including inhibitory neurons in CA1 S.O. and S.LM. (43±5% Sst+, 0% Pvalb+) and a novel excitatory projection from superficial subiculum (>33% of intrahippocampal projections, GAD1-negative, pyramidal morphology, CaMKII+).
evaluation: Claims C5, C41-C49, C80-C81 are supported by comprehensive anatomical data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1. The identification is based on multiple converging lines of evidence: GAD1 colocalization, immunohistochemistry for Sst/Pvalb, morphology, and AAV tracing with cell-type specific promoters. The quantification (n=189 cells, 3 animals) is adequate.

result: Using cre-on and cre-off AAV vectors in Calb1cre mice enabled differential retrograde labeling from superficial vs deep CA1 pyramidal neurons, revealing that both receive equal CA3 input but deep CA1 neurons receive substantially greater LEC-3 input.
evaluation: Claims C50-C52 are supported by the experimental design shown in Figure 5A-B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A. The approach is validated by citations to previous lower-throughput studies (Li et al., 2017; Masurkar et al., 2017) showing consistent results. The cre-off mechanism using SEO is clearly illustrated and demonstrated.

result: Retrograde labeling from hippocampal inhibitory neurons using intersectional genetic strategies revealed a small population of long-range inhibitory projection neurons located preferentially in EC layers 5a and 6, with the deeper cortical layers giving rise to both inhibitory and excitatory hippocampal projections.
evaluation: Claims C53-C59 are supported by data in Figure 5C-G using two complementary approaches (mDLX promoter and Dlx5/6flpE × Ai65 intersectional genetics). The identification of layer-specific localization is novel (C54), though existence was previously reported. The quantification shows clear layer-specific distribution patterns. Sample sizes (n=8 sections/3 animals) are adequate.

result: Bicistronic CVS-N2c vectors using the endogenous N-P linker sequence efficiently express individual proteins in compartment-specific manner, enabling dual labeling of nuclear and cytoplasmic or synaptic compartments.
evaluation: Claims C60-C61, C82 are supported by data in Figure 6A-B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The approach is adapted from prior work (Osakada et al., 2018) and demonstrated with multiple protein combinations. FACS analysis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C) shows no substantial differences in expression levels between mono- and bicistronic vectors.

result: Bicistronic CVS-N2c vectors expressing tdTomato and oChIEF enable reliable optogenetic activation at high frequencies (up to 100 Hz) as early as 6-7 days post-injection, with recorded neurons showing healthy resting membrane potentials (-55 to -75 mV), though cellular health deteriorates in vitro after 10 days.
evaluation: Claims C62-C65, C83-C85 are supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 6C-E. The improved performance is attributed to both the bicistronic design and the ChIEF variant (C84), appropriately acknowledging multiple contributing factors. The exclusion criteria (3/21 cells with Vm > -55 mV) is clearly stated. The demonstration of circuit mapping applications (Figure 6E) validates utility.

result: In vivo two-photon calcium imaging of GCaMP8m-labeled V1 neurons demonstrates that CVS-N2c vectors enable functional recording from day 7 to day 16 post-injection, with neurons maintaining normal physiological properties including stable signal-to-noise ratios, direction tuning, and similar response properties between 1st and 2nd order neurons.
evaluation: Claims C6, C66-C72, C78 are supported by comprehensive in vivo imaging data in Figure 7. The time course is well-documented (n=3 animals), showing stable functional properties from day 7-16. The quantification of direction selectivity, SNR (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), and tuning properties provides strong evidence for maintained neuronal health. This addresses a key limitation of rabies vectors.

result: The new packaging system demonstrates that superior CVS-N2c labeling efficiency stems from the viral strain itself rather than N2A cell production, and the co-expression of TVA/envA minimizes native-coat contamination, providing a fast, simple, and highly effective approach for circuit mapping.
evaluation: Claims C30, C73-C75, C86 represent the key conceptual conclusions supported by the comparative experiments in Figure 3 and the overall system characterization. The hypothesis that efficiency stems from the strain rather than production method (C73) is directly tested and confirmed. The design rationale for TVA/envA co-expression (C74) is validated by contamination data.

result: It remains possible that packaging CVS-N2c vectors in N2A cells would result in reduced neurotoxicity compared with vectors packaged in non-neuronal cell lines, though this was not directly tested.
evaluation: Claim C79 explicitly acknowledges uncertainty as no direct comparison of neurotoxicity between N2A and BHK-eT production was performed. While C78 shows maintained viability for 16 days with BHK-eT-produced vectors, the lack of head-to-head comparison prevents definitive conclusions about relative neurotoxicity. This is appropriately stated as speculation in the manuscript.

result: Background claims establishing the context and limitations of existing rabies tracing technologies, including the properties of SAD B19 and CVS-N2c strains, and the rationale for developing improved production methods.
evaluation: Claims C7-C16, C20, C36, C59 are background statements supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Wickersham et al., 2007; Reardon et al., 2016; Albisetti et al., 2017; Osakada and Callaway, 2013; etc.). These provide necessary context for understanding the significance of the new system. The characterization of existing methods' limitations is well-documented in the cited literature.
